items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: So from about, oh, about four months we toured with Josephine Baker

ctx.x: Well, when did you go into -- you started to talk about that last time. When did you go into the studios?

Well, 1950, when Josephine Baker first came over to the States. Buddy Rich, we were backing Josephine Baker. He became her musical director. And the band. So from about, oh, about four months we toured with Josephine Baker and then Buddy, you know, it was just theaters. Buddy wanted to play, naturally everybody wanted to play. But Buddy Rich is not the type to be an accompanist, you know. So he split and I became

the trumpet player with her, you know. And then she went back to Paris and came back the next year and I became her musical director. That was in 1952. Oh, I toured with her for a long time. Went to Mexico City six months.

items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: she suggested that we do a little act together... We rehearsed it and got it down very well. And she would go around me and dance while I would play the trumpet. And it became part of the show.

ctx.x: Roland played with you for…it wasn’t just that one period. He stayed with you for a while.
Yes, he played with me off and on. Then, after that I went with Josephine Baker.
Can we backtrack and little and discuss how you settled in Los Angeles and how you ended up making this your home.
